llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated purpose (a multi-agent engineering toolkit) but contains several incoherent or risky elements — notably an install-by-curl|bash pattern, many bundled code files that expect local system access (cookies, keychain, a persistent Chromium daemon and Bun), and a detected prompt-injection pattern — you should inspect the installer and runtime scripts before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (multi-agent engineering team with a headless browser) aligns with the included code (browser daemon, QA tools, skills). However the skill metadata claims 'instruction-only' / no required binaries/env but the repository contains substantial native/local tooling (install.sh, bun-based build, browser daemon, Chrome extension, cookie import) that legitimately require Bun, Chromium/Playwright, and local file/Keychain access. The lack of declared runtime requirements (binaries, env) is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs users/agents to run curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh | bash or to clone the repo and run the installer; the code and docs describe copying Chromium cookie DBs, decrypting cookies (Keychain/DPAPI/gnome-keyring), running a persistent localhost daemon that reads/writes ~/.founderclaw and symlinks into ~/.agents/skills, and restarting the gateway. These instructions cause broad local access (files, keychain prompts, daemon binding to localhost) and may modify agent config — more than an innocuous prompt-only skill. The SKILL.md also contains a pre-scan 'system-prompt-override' pattern which could indicate prompt-injection content.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec declared in registry, yet SKILL.md recommends piping a remote raw GitHub script to bash (curl | bash). While GitHub raw is a known host, piping remote scripts to shell is high-risk because arbitrary code will be executed locally. The repo contains install.sh/uninstall.sh and build steps that expect Bun and a compiled binary; the registry metadata did not declare these dependencies, which is an incoherence and increases risk because users/agents may run the installer without verifying prerequisites or contents.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry shows no required env vars or credentials, but source/docs reference use of an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for tests and describe operations that require sensitive local access (reading browser cookie DBs, prompting macOS Keychain, writing encrypted state to ~/.founderclaw, creating symlinks in ~/.agents/skills). Requesting access to cookies/Keychain and modifying agent config is proportionate to the claimed browser/QA capabilities only if the user understands and consents — but the absence of declared requirements and the remote installer suggestion are inconsistent and warrant caution.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true, and autonomous invocation is allowed (default). The installer will create persistent files and directories (e.g., ~/.founderclaw, ~/.agents/skills/founderclaw symlinks), starts a long-lived daemon, and can restart the gateway; that's expected for a tool that provides a persistent browser daemon and a 29-skill suite. This is legitimate functionality but increases blast radius — installing modifies local agent configuration and persists services that will run later.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- Inspect the installer first: do NOT run curl | bash blindly. Review install.sh and uninstall.sh in the repo (or open the GitHub project in your browser) and search for remote downloads, exec/spawn of arbitrary commands, or network endpoints that receive data.
- Understand local access: this package copies Chromium cookie DB files, prompts your OS keychain, and runs a persistent local daemon that binds to localhost and writes ~/.founderclaw and symlinks into ~/.agents/skills. If you don't want a tool to access browser cookies or modify your agent config, do not install it.
- Dependency mismatch: the registry declares no required binaries/env, but the code expects Bun, Chromium/Playwright tooling, and may use an LLM API key in tests. Confirm you can provide/verify those dependencies and that the installer will not install surprising system components.
- Prompt-injection signal: a 'system-prompt-override' pattern was detected in SKILL.md. Read SKILL.md and templated preambles to ensure nothing attempts to override agent/system prompts or exfiltrate context.
- Safer install options: (1) clone the repo and inspect scripts locally before running them; (2) run install in a disposable VM/container; (3) run uninstall.sh in a test environment to verify it removes what it created; (4) prefer manual installation of only the components you trust (e.g., enable only the non-browse skills if you don't need cookie access).

If you want, I can: (a) fetch and summarize the contents of install.sh and highlight risky commands, (b) list places that access Keychain/cookie DBs or external endpoints, or (c) suggest a safe sequence to audit and run the installer in a sandbox.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The SKILL.md pre-scan flagged 'system-prompt-override' patterns. A multi-agent tooling repo will include many policy/ethos docs, but explicit system-prompt override content inside a skill file is not expected and could indicate prompt-injection attempts or overly broad embedded directives. Inspect SKILL.md and any templates for code that attempts to alter system-level agent prompts or behavior.
